title: Director of Operations

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: Responsible for manufacturing efficiency, quality control, and warranty claim management across Ultraflex's 500,000+ square feet of global stock holding space and five North American warehouses. This role directly experiences the operational pain of product failures: customer complaints about fading, cracking, and weather damage on outdoor installations drive warranty replacements, damage customer relationships, and inflate operational costs. Tedlar solves their operational KPIs: (1) drastically reduce warranty claim rates by preventing UV degradation, yellowing, and weather-related failures that plague current 1-3 year outdoor materials, (2) lower total cost of quality through fewer returns and replacements, (3) improve customer satisfaction scores by delivering products that actually withstand harsh weather conditions as marketed, and (4) simplify quality assurance—Tedlar's proven 60+ year track record reduces variability and performance uncertainty. Given Ultraflex markets materials with 'additional strength and stability under harsh weather conditions,' this role needs protective films that actually deliver on that promise to reduce the operational burden of underperforming products in the field.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: The Director of Operations at Ultraflex oversees manufacturing, quality control, distribution logistics across five North American warehouses and 500,000+ square feet of global inventory space, and likely owns warranty/returns management. They manage operational costs, quality metrics, and customer satisfaction for Ultraflex's substrate product lines. This role reports to C-suite (likely COO or President) and manages quality assurance, warehouse, and potentially production teams. They influence decisions on supplier selection for materials and protective films, particularly when quality issues or warranty claims create operational burden. While they may not have final authority on new product development, they hold significant influence when operational pain points (high return rates, customer complaints, warranty costs) reach critical levels.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: For Ultraflex's outdoor-exposed products—building wraps, barricade graphics, outdoor banners, and fence graphics—Tedlar directly addresses their operational challenges. Their current outdoor banner materials last 1-3 years, creating a predictable cycle of warranty claims and customer dissatisfaction when installations fail prematurely due to UV degradation, fading, or weather damage. Tedlar as an overlaminate would extend the lifespan of these products to 12-20+ years, dramatically reducing warranty exposure. Specific use cases relevant to their operations: (1) Building wraps and architectural graphics where premature failure creates costly removal/replacement and damages customer relationships, (2) Outdoor banners and fence graphics that currently degrade within 1-3 years despite marketing claims of harsh weather resistance, and (3) Transit and display applications where graffiti resistance reduces maintenance callbacks. The operations team would immediately benefit from fewer quality complaints, reduced warranty processing costs, lower inventory turnover for replacement materials, and improved customer retention.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: This role likely owns KPIs around: warranty claim rate, cost of quality (returns/replacements), customer satisfaction scores, inventory turnover efficiency, and manufacturing yield. They personally care about reducing the volume of customer complaints that flow through their quality team, minimizing costly warranty replacements that strain warehouse operations and damage margins, and delivering products that perform as marketed to avoid operational firefighting. The current gap—marketing 'harsh weather resistance' while products actually fail in 1-3 years outdoors—creates daily operational headaches. Tedlar's UV protection (no yellowing, fading, cracking) and weather resistance (-70°F to 230°F range) directly solve the quality failures that generate warranty claims. Additionally, graffiti resistance reduces post-installation service calls and maintenance costs. By drastically reducing warranty rates, Tedlar lowers their total cost of quality, frees up warehouse capacity previously allocated to replacement inventory, and improves customer satisfaction metrics that reflect on their operational performance reviews.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Ultraflex just launched their VorTex Soft Signage line with four new ReSource products in November 2025, indicating active product development cycles and openness to product enhancements. They're exhibiting at PRINTING United Expo 2025 (October 22-24 in Orlando) with a fully built 80s arcade-themed booth, demonstrating significant investment in market presence and product showcase opportunities. This timing creates urgency: if they're preparing trade show demonstrations and marketing materials for their outdoor graphics portfolio, NOW is when they need to address the durability gap before making performance claims they can't deliver on. Recent product launches also mean their operations team is likely dealing with early customer feedback and establishing quality benchmarks—an ideal window to introduce Tedlar as a protective solution that ensures new products meet durability expectations. The gap between their 1-3 year outdoor lifespan and industry-leading competitors creates competitive pressure that makes this conversation timely.

personalization_hooks.hook: Ultraflex markets materials with 'additional strength and stability under harsh weather conditions,' but their outdoor banners typically last only 1-3 years—creating a disconnect between marketing promises and field performance that generates warranty claims
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open with empathy about the operational challenge of managing warranty claims when outdoor products don't deliver on weather resistance promises. Position Tedlar as the solution that aligns product performance with their marketing claims, reducing the operational burden of returns and customer complaints. Frame it as: 'How do you currently handle warranty claims when outdoor installations fail before customers expect them to?'

personalization_hooks.hook: Ultraflex operates 500,000+ square feet of global stock holding space across five North American warehouses—warranty replacements and returns consume valuable inventory capacity and logistics resources
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead with cost of quality angle: calculate the warehouse space, labor, and logistics costs tied to processing warranty claims and storing replacement inventory for failed outdoor products. Position Tedlar as a way to reclaim operational efficiency by eliminating the majority of weather-related failures. Example opener: 'What percentage of your warehouse throughput is dedicated to warranty replacements for outdoor products that degrade prematurely?'

personalization_hooks.hook: Recent VorTex Soft Signage line launch (November 2025) and upcoming PRINTING United Expo presence (October 2025) indicate active product development cycles—ideal timing to enhance outdoor product portfolio before next trade show cycle
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference their recent product innovation and trade show investment, positioning Tedlar as a strategic enhancement for their outdoor graphics portfolio ahead of major industry events. Frame as: 'As you prepare for PRINTING United and scale the new VorTex line, have you considered how protective overlaminates could differentiate your outdoor products and reduce post-launch warranty exposure?' Suggests collaboration opportunity rather than pointing out current shortcomings.

recommended_approach: Lead with operational cost reduction and warranty claim pain points, not product features. Start by acknowledging the challenge of managing quality when outdoor products face harsh conditions, then quantify the operational impact (warranty processing costs, customer service burden, inventory tied up in replacements). Position Tedlar as solving an operational efficiency problem first, product performance problem second. Avoid leading with technical specs—this role cares about metrics like warranty rate reduction and cost savings more than film chemistry. Offer a brief call to discuss their current warranty trends and how other substrates manufacturers have reduced claims using protective overlaminates.
